It is often compared to the qualities of a well-loved and respected leader who is able to unite and bring people together, creating an environment of peace and unity, as the name suggests, one who attracts people towards him.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (Conquest of Egypt), 2/77. The name Murghib carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Murghib ibn Masruq al-Fihri, a Berber chieftain, led a rebellion against the Arab Muslim rule in Egypt. He was defeated and killed by the Muslim general, 'Amr ibn al-'As.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Khaldun, Al-'Ibar, 2/122. The name Murghib carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Murghib ibn Sa'id al-Buzuri, a Marinid Berber ruler, led the invasion of the Maghreb region (North Africa) against the Hafsids. He was eventually defeated and killed by the Hafsid ruler, Abu 'Abd Allah II.
